issue_context.title: XNodeReader.GetAttribute(int) should throw on invalid indices
issue_context.body:
Note: this class is internal but this method is accessible through XmlReader's public surface which can be created with i.e. XNode.CreateReader.

All XmlReader implementations except XNodeReader throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException on invalid indices. This specific class returns null though. Documentation of XmlReader says that ArgumentOutOfRange is expected behavior.

Also same method returns null when reader state is not in interactive mode - likely this should be replaced with InvalidOperationException.

Found with nullable annotations.

I think we should fix this for consistency but there is no urgency here considering this issue has been there for years and no one has complained.

review_comments: I've missed this before but shouldn't last line of this method also throw ArgumentOutOfRange instead of returning null? The last line is supposedly out of range on the upper side

Couldn't the `index <0 ` check extended to a range check of AttributeCount? I.e. `if(index < 0 || index >= AttributeCount)`? However since AttributeCount includes the same logic as here, this would run the same iteration code twice in the worst case.
Otherwise yes, the last line should throw as well.
Updated and moved the failing tests to actual test cases as well.
can you add a test case where XML element has exactly one attribute and you read index=1?
Isn't it a breaking change? I am OK with this change, even it is documented that it will throw this exception in this case, but i guess we need to mark this PR as breaking change at least
I've added the label so that we make sure to document this.

I do not really like this change, it might be the expected behavior but i see the other overloads above doing same check and still returning null.
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/32f5b72b2bde2aa6fcf4d0d202a898e9cb8233ce/src/libraries/System.Private.Xml.Linq/src/System/Xml/Linq/XNodeReader.cs#L468-L471
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/32f5b72b2bde2aa6fcf4d0d202a898e9cb8233ce/src/libraries/System.Private.Xml.Linq/src/System/Xml/Linq/XNodeReader.cs#L514-L517
1. i think it is more breaking change
2. i think this behavior should stay the same as the other overloads

considering the AttributeCount returns 0: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/32f5b72b2bde2aa6fcf4d0d202a898e9cb8233ce/src/libraries/System.Private.Xml.Linq/src/System/Xml/Linq/XNodeReader.cs#L44

IMO we should also throw ArgumentOutOfRange. Other overloads do not throw because they don't throw I think
(note that two examples you pasted return nullable so it makes sense to return null)

> IMO we should also throw ArgumentOutOfRange. 

I would prefer the InvalidOperationException than ArgumentOutOfRange as it was not caused from argument

> (note that two examples you pasted return nullable so it makes sense to return null)

Ah, didn't notice that, another option could be to return `string.Empty` which i see for other methods returning non null string, and might be less breaking, but i will let you decide what to do, overall i am OK with this PR changes
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/32f5b72b2bde2aa6fcf4d0d202a898e9cb8233ce/src/libraries/System.Private.Xml.Linq/src/System/Xml/Linq/XNodeReader.cs#L247-L252

the namespace URI is a bit different since null and empty string are equivalent for all (or at least most) XML APIs.

For the InvalidOperation vs ArgumentOutOfRange I'm ok either way. In the interactive mode you shouldn't be calling the method at all so InvalidOperation is accurate. Might be worth to match behavior of other XML readers.
